sectionTitle: What changed beyond the sales office

primary.headline: Why Buying a New Home Is Now Cheaper Than an Existing One in Many Markets
primary.summary: Reporting cites recent market data showing the long-standing new-construction price premium over resale homes has narrowed or inverted in a number of U.S. metros, driven by builders' sustained use of rate buydowns, price cuts, and closing-cost credits to move inventory -- the same mechanism this sweep tracks daily in Austin. The piece frames this as a structural shift in buyer leverage rather than a one-off sale.
primary.buyerImplication: Directly validates what this sweep's own data has shown for months: Austin-area builders are carrying median advertised incentives around $25,000-$32,000 across 30+ active builders, with several offers exceeding $85,000-$105,000 on specific communities. Buyers comparing a new build to a comparable resale listing should run the full cost comparison (price, incentive value, HOA, warranty, and lender-tied rate terms) rather than assuming resale is cheaper by default.
primary.buyerAction: Before ruling out new construction as the pricier option, get the builder's current incentive-adjusted price in writing and compare it against a comparable resale listing's true closing cost -- not just list price. Use this sweep's Biggest Live Dollar Offers table as a starting point for which Austin-area builders are currently most aggressive.
primary.confidence: High confidence -- FOX 7 Austin reporting, published 2026-10-04; re-verified 2026-10-12 (9th consecutive day in rotation) after a fresh search pass checked two candidates: a Community Impact piece on a Georgetown builder that is paid sponsored content credited to the builder (rejected on source quality), and an independent but 14-month-old Georgetown community story (rejected on recency). Recency score stepped down to 5; total 76 remains above the 70-point publish bar. Market figures are as characterized in the source reporting.
